blocks.en_html: Model for Inter-Domain Routing
blocks.zh_html: 域间路由(inter-domain routing)模型

blocks.en: Inter-Domain Routing
blocks.en_html: Inter-Domain Routing
blocks.zh_html: 域间路由(Inter-Domain Routing)

blocks.en: Recall from earlier that routing is performed in a network of networks. We’ve seen distance-vector and link-state protocols that can be used to implement intra-domain routing, which allows packets to be sent within a local network.
blocks.en_html: Recall from earlier that routing is performed in a network of networks. We’ve seen distance-vector and link-state protocols that can be used to implement intra-domain routing, which allows packets to be sent within a local network.
blocks.zh_html: 回想一下，路由(routing)是在网络的网络(network of networks)中进行的。我们已经学习了可用于实现域内路由(intra-domain routing)的距离向量(distance-vector)和链路状态(link-state)协议，它们让分组(packets)可以在本地网络(local network)内部发送。

blocks.en: In this section, we’ll build a model that will allow us to define inter-domain routing protocols, which can send packets between different local networks. We’ll also see how inter-domain and intra-domain routing protocols combine to allow packets to be sent to any host in any network.
blocks.en_html: In this section, we’ll build a model that will allow us to define inter-domain routing protocols, which can send packets between different local networks. We’ll also see how inter-domain and intra-domain routing protocols combine to allow packets to be sent to any host in any network.
blocks.zh_html: 在本节中，我们会构造一个模型(model)，用来定义域间路由协议(inter-domain routing protocols)，它让分组可以在不同本地网络(local networks)之间发送。我们还会看到域间路由和域内路由协议如何协同工作，让分组可以到达任何网络中的任何主机(host)。

blocks.en: Defining Autonomous Systems
blocks.en_html: Defining Autonomous Systems
blocks.zh_html: 定义自治系统(Defining Autonomous Systems)

blocks.en: We can formalize the notion of a local network by defining an autonomous system (AS), which is one or more local network(s) all run by the same operator. For example, within a company like Google, there might be a local network for employee computers, and another local network for data centers, but both networks are controlled by the same company. The operator can deploy a single intra-domain routing protocol to send messages between machines on any of those local networks. Sometimes, the term domain is used to informally refer to an AS, though this term is also used in other protocols, so we will say AS when possible.
blocks.en_html: We can formalize the notion of a local network by defining an autonomous system (AS), which is one or more local network(s) all run by the same operator. For example, within a company like Google, there might be a local network for employee computers, and another local network for data centers, but both networks are controlled by the same company. The operator can deploy a single intra-domain routing protocol to send messages between machines on any of those local networks. Sometimes, the term domain is used to informally refer to an AS, though this term is also used in other protocols, so we will say AS when possible.
blocks.zh_html: 我们可以通过定义自治系统(autonomous system, AS)来形式化(formalize)本地网络(local network)的概念。一个 AS 是由同一个运营方(operator)管理的一个或多个本地网络。例如，在 Google 这样的公司内部，可能有员工电脑的本地网络和数据中心(data centers)的另一个本地网络，但两个网络都由同一家公司控制。运营方可以部署统一的域内路由协议(intra-domain routing protocol)，在这些本地网络中的机器之间发送消息。术语域(domain)有时被非正式地用来指代 AS，但这个词也在其他协议中使用，所以我们尽量用 AS。

blocks.en: To think about routing packets between autonomous systems, we can abstract away all of the individual routers and hosts within the AS, and treat the AS as a single entity. Then, we can draw a graph where each node represents an AS, and edges between two ASes represents a connection between them. This graph is sometimes called the inter-domain topology or an AS graph.
blocks.en_html: To think about routing packets between autonomous systems, we can abstract away all of the individual routers and hosts within the AS, and treat the AS as a single entity. Then, we can draw a graph where each node represents an AS, and edges between two ASes represents a connection between them. This graph is sometimes called the inter-domain topology or an AS graph.
blocks.zh_html: 为了思考如何在自治系统(autonomous systems)之间路由分组，我们可以抽象掉 AS 内部的所有单独路由器和主机，把 AS 当作一个整体对待。然后，我们可以画一个图(graph)，其中每个节点代表一个 AS，两个 AS 之间的边(edge)表示它们之间的连接。这个图有时被称为域间拓扑(inter-domain topology)或AS 图(AS graph)。

blocks.en: Brief History of Autonomous Systems
blocks.en_html: Brief History of Autonomous Systems
blocks.zh_html: 自治系统简史(Brief History of Autonomous Systems)

blocks.en: In real life, an organization called the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) manages a global list of all autonomous systems that exist in the Internet. In order to be an AS, you must register with this organization and receive a unique autonomous system number (ASN).
blocks.en_html: In real life, an organization called the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) manages a global list of all autonomous systems that exist in the Internet. In order to be an AS, you must register with this organization and receive a unique autonomous system number (ASN).
blocks.zh_html: 在现实中，一个名为互联网号码分配局(Internet Assigned Numbers Authority, IANA)的组织负责管理互联网上所有自治系统(autonomous systems)的全局列表。要成为一个 AS，你必须向该组织注册，并获得一个唯一的自治系统编号(autonomous system number, ASN)。

blocks.en: Fun fact: In the early days, the IANA was administered manually by a single person, Jon Postel. This meant that anybody in the world who wanted to register a new AS would have to ask for his approval.
blocks.en_html: Fun fact: In the early days, the IANA was administered manually by a single person, Jon Postel. This meant that anybody in the world who wanted to register a new AS would have to ask for his approval.
blocks.zh_html: 有趣的事实：在早期，IANA 由一个人，Jon Postel，手动管理。这意味着世界上任何想要注册新 AS 的人都必须征得他的批准。

blocks.en: Today, there are over 90,000 autonomous systems, with the United States having the most ASes of any country.
blocks.en_html: Today, there are over 90,000 autonomous systems, with the United States having the most ASes of any country.
blocks.zh_html: 如今，有超过 90,000 个自治系统(autonomous systems)，其中美国拥有的 AS 数量最多。

blocks.en: Fun fact: UC Berkeley has ASN 25, which is a remarkably low number given that there are so many ASNs. This reflects the fact that UC Berkeley received its ASN very early in the Internet’s history (in the 1980s).
blocks.en_html: Fun fact: UC Berkeley has ASN 25, which is a remarkably low number given that there are so many ASNs. This reflects the fact that UC Berkeley received its ASN very early in the Internet’s history (in the 1980s).
blocks.zh_html: 有趣的事实：加州大学伯克利分校(UC Berkeley)的 ASN 是 25，考虑到有这么多 ASN，这是一个非常小的数字。这反映了 UC Berkeley 在互联网历史早期（1980 年代）就获得了它的 ASN。

blocks.en: Types of ASes
blocks.en_html: Types of ASes
blocks.zh_html: AS 的类型(Types of ASes)

blocks.en: Recall that when modeling the network for intra-domain routing, we made a distinction between end hosts and routers. We’ll make a similar distinction for inter-domain routing by defining two types of ASes.
blocks.en_html: Recall that when modeling the network for intra-domain routing, we made a distinction between end hosts and routers. We’ll make a similar distinction for inter-domain routing by defining two types of ASes.
blocks.zh_html: 回想一下，在为域内路由(intra-domain routing)建模网络时，我们区分了终端主机(end hosts)和路由器(routers)。对于域间路由(inter-domain routing)，我们通过定义两种类型的 AS 来做类似的区分。

blocks.en: A stub autonomous system only exists to provide Internet connectivity to the hosts in its local networks. A stub AS only sends and receives packets on behalf of hosts that are inside the AS, and does not forward packets between different ASes. These are analogous to the end hosts in our intra-domain routing model, which only sent and received their own packets and did not forward other people’s packets.
blocks.en_html: A stub autonomous system only exists to provide Internet connectivity to the hosts in its local networks. A stub AS only sends and receives packets on behalf of hosts that are inside the AS, and does not forward packets between different ASes. These are analogous to the end hosts in our intra-domain routing model, which only sent and received their own packets and did not forward other people’s packets.
blocks.zh_html: 一个末梢自治系统(stub autonomous system)只为其本地网络(local networks)中的主机(hosts)提供互联网连接(Internet connectivity)。末梢 AS(stub AS)只代表其内部的主机发送和接收分组(packets)，不负责在不同 AS 之间转发分组。这类似于我们域内路由模型中的终端主机(end hosts)，它们只发送和接收自己的分组，不转发其他人的分组。

blocks.en: Real-life examples of stub ASes include non-Internet companies (e.g. a bank offering connectivity to its employees) or universities (e.g. UC Berkeley offering connectivity to its students and employees). These organizations are not responsible for carrying Internet traffic from other organizations. The vast majority of ASes in the world are stub ASes.
blocks.en_html: Real-life examples of stub ASes include non-Internet companies (e.g. a bank offering connectivity to its employees) or universities (e.g. UC Berkeley offering connectivity to its students and employees). These organizations are not responsible for carrying Internet traffic from other organizations. The vast majority of ASes in the world are stub ASes.
blocks.zh_html: 现实中的末梢 AS(stub AS)例子包括非互联网公司（例如为员工提供网络连接的银行）或大学（例如为师生提供网络连接的 UC Berkeley）。这些组织不负责承载来自其他组织的互联网流量。世界上绝大多数 AS 都是末梢 AS。

blocks.en: By contrast, a transit autonomous system forwards packets on behalf of other ASes. A transit AS could carry a packet between two different ASes by receiving and forwarding that packet.
blocks.en_html: By contrast, a transit autonomous system forwards packets on behalf of other ASes. A transit AS could carry a packet between two different ASes by receiving and forwarding that packet.
blocks.zh_html: 相反，一个中转自治系统(transit autonomous system)代表其他 AS 转发分组。一个中转 AS(transit AS)可以通过接收并转发分组，在两个不同的 AS 之间传输分组。

blocks.en: Transit ASes correspond to real-life companies whose business includes selling Internet connectivity to other organizations. Real-life examples of transit ASes include AT&T and Verizon, which are companies that you can pay to offer you Internet connectivity. Some transit ASes like AT&T are global, with infrastructure around the world. Others might be specific to a region, like Sonic, an Internet service provider that only forwards traffic to and from California.
blocks.en_html: Transit ASes correspond to real-life companies whose business includes selling Internet connectivity to other organizations. Real-life examples of transit ASes include AT&T and Verizon, which are companies that you can pay to offer you Internet connectivity. Some transit ASes like AT&T are global, with infrastructure around the world. Others might be specific to a region, like Sonic, an Internet service provider that only forwards traffic to and from California.
blocks.zh_html: 中转 AS(transit AS)对应于现实中那些业务包括向其他组织出售互联网连接的公司。现实中的例子包括 AT&T 和 Verizon，你可以付费从这些公司获得互联网连接。一些中转 AS，如 AT&T，是全球性的，在世界各地都有基础设施。其他一些可能只针对某个地区，例如 Sonic，一家只转发进出加利福尼亚州流量的互联网服务提供商(Internet service provider)。

blocks.en: Note that a transit AS can still contain end hosts that send and receive packets of their own. Nevertheless, a transit AS is similar to the routers in our intra-domain routing model, which received other users’ packets and forwarded them on behalf of users.
blocks.en_html: Note that a transit AS can still contain end hosts that send and receive packets of their own. Nevertheless, a transit AS is similar to the routers in our intra-domain routing model, which received other users’ packets and forwarded them on behalf of users.
blocks.zh_html: 注意，中转 AS(transit AS)仍然可以包含发送和接收自己分组的主机(hosts)。不过，中转 AS 类似于我们域内路由模型中的路由器(routers)，它们接收其他用户的分组并代表用户转发。

blocks.en: This model of stub and transit ASes is what we’ll use in these notes, though sometimes, the classification in real life can be less well-defined. For example, major tech companies like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon control massive ASes that carry as much traffic as transit ASes (and maybe even more). Because their primary role is to carry traffic to and from their services (e.g. receive Google search requests and send search results), they could be classifed as stub ASes. In recent years, though, these companies have also offered to carry traffic between ASes, so they could arguably be classified as transit ASes as well.
blocks.en_html: This model of stub and transit ASes is what we’ll use in these notes, though sometimes, the classification in real life can be less well-defined. For example, major tech companies like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon control massive ASes that carry as much traffic as transit ASes (and maybe even more). Because their primary role is to carry traffic to and from their services (e.g. receive Google search requests and send search results), they could be classifed as stub ASes. In recent years, though, these companies have also offered to carry traffic between ASes, so they could arguably be classified as transit ASes as well.
blocks.zh_html: 本笔记将使用这种末梢(stub)和中转(transit)AS 模型，尽管现实中的分类有时不那么明确。例如，Google、Microsoft 和 Amazon 等大型科技公司控制着庞大的 AS，承载的流量不亚于中转 AS（甚至可能更多）。由于它们的主要角色是承载进出其服务的流量（例如接收 Google 搜索请求并发送搜索结果），它们可以被归类为末梢 AS。但近年来，这些公司也开始提供 AS 之间的流量承载服务，因此也可以说它们属于中转 AS。

blocks.en: Inter-Domain Topology Is Defined by Business Relationships
blocks.en_html: Inter-Domain Topology Is Defined by Business Relationships
blocks.zh_html: 域间拓扑由商业关系定义(Inter-Domain Topology Is Defined by Business Relationships)

blocks.en: In our inter-domain topology, we draw an edge between two ASes if they exchange traffic. What causes two real-life organizations, such as a local bank and Verizon, to agree to exchange traffic? The edges in the AS are defined by real-world business relationships between ASes.
blocks.en_html: In our inter-domain topology, we draw an edge between two ASes if they exchange traffic. What causes two real-life organizations, such as a local bank and Verizon, to agree to exchange traffic? The edges in the AS are defined by real-world business relationships between ASes.
blocks.zh_html: 在我们的域间拓扑(inter-domain topology)中，如果两个 AS 交换流量，我们就在它们之间画一条边(edge)。什么原因会让两个现实中的组织，比如一家本地银行和 Verizon，同意交换流量？AS 图中的边是由 AS 之间真实的商业关系(business relationships)定义的。

blocks.en: There are two possible ways that a pair of ASes could be related.
blocks.en_html: There are two possible ways that a pair of ASes could be related.
blocks.zh_html: 一对 AS 之间可能存在两种关系。

blocks.en: A pair of ASes could be involved in a customer-provider relationship. In real life, the customer is paying for service, and the provider is offering connectivity in exchange for money. For example, the local bank AS could be the customer, paying the provider, Verizon, for Internet services.
blocks.en_html: A pair of ASes could be involved in a customer-provider relationship. In real life, the customer is paying for service, and the provider is offering connectivity in exchange for money. For example, the local bank AS could be the customer, paying the provider, Verizon, for Internet services.
blocks.zh_html: 一对 AS 之间可能存在客户-提供商关系(customer-provider relationship)。在现实中，客户(customer)为服务付费，提供商(provider)提供连接以换取金钱。例如，本地银行 AS 可以是客户，向提供商 Verizon 付费以获取互联网服务。

blocks.en: A pair of ASes could also be involved in a peer relationship. Two peer ASes usually send each other a roughly equal amount of traffic. In real life, two ASes could agree to become peers by signing a legal contract between companies. Usually, the two peers agree to not pay each other for connectivity services, as long as the traffic sent in either direction is roughly equal.
blocks.en_html: A pair of ASes could also be involved in a peer relationship. Two peer ASes usually send each other a roughly equal amount of traffic. In real life, two ASes could agree to become peers by signing a legal contract between companies. Usually, the two peers agree to not pay each other for connectivity services, as long as the traffic sent in either direction is roughly equal.
blocks.zh_html: 一对 AS 之间也可能存在对等关系(peer relationship)。两个对等 AS(peer ASes)通常互相发送大致相等的流量。在现实中，两个 AS 可以通过签署公司间的法律合同来成为对等体。通常情况下，两个对等体同意不互相支付连接费用，只要双向发送的流量大致相等。

blocks.en: AS Graph with Business Relationships
blocks.en_html: AS Graph with Business Relationships
blocks.zh_html: 带商业关系的 AS 图(AS Graph with Business Relationships)

blocks.en: We can draw these relationships into the AS graph by adding arrows to the graph. A directed edge points from the provider to the customer. An undirected edge connects two peers. Note that the graph can contain both directed and undirected edges (not all edges need to have arrows).
blocks.en_html: We can draw these relationships into the AS graph by adding arrows to the graph. A directed edge points from the provider to the customer. An undirected edge connects two peers. Note that the graph can contain both directed and undirected edges (not all edges need to have arrows).
blocks.zh_html: 我们可以通过在图(graph)中添加箭头来将这些关系画入 AS 图。有向边(directed edge)从提供商(provider)指向客户(customer)。无向边(undirected edge)连接两个对等体(peers)。注意，图中可以同时包含有向边和无向边，并非所有边都需要有箭头。

blocks.en: Stub ASes in the graph are only customers. They have incoming edges, showing who provides them with connectivity. However, they don’t have any outgoing edges, because they don’t provide connectivity to others.
blocks.en_html: Stub ASes in the graph are only customers. They have incoming edges, showing who provides them with connectivity. However, they don’t have any outgoing edges, because they don’t provide connectivity to others.
blocks.zh_html: 图中的末梢 AS(stub ASes)只是客户。它们有入边(incoming edges)，显示谁为它们提供连接。然而，它们没有出边(outgoing edges)，因为她们不为其他人提供连接。

blocks.en: By contrast, transit ASes in the graph are the providers. Their outgoing arrows show that they are selling connectivity to other organizations.
blocks.en_html: By contrast, transit ASes in the graph are the providers. Their outgoing arrows show that they are selling connectivity to other organizations.
blocks.zh_html: 相反，图中的中转 AS(transit ASes)是提供商(providers)。它们的出箭头表示它们正在向其他组织出售连接服务。

blocks.en: Note that the direction of the arrow does not tell us anything about what direction the packets are being sent. In fact, packets can be sent in both directions even along a directed edge. The customer often pays the provider for the ability to send packets to and receive packets from the rest of the Internet.
blocks.en_html: Note that the direction of the arrow does not tell us anything about what direction the packets are being sent. In fact, packets can be sent in both directions even along a directed edge. The customer often pays the provider for the ability to send packets to and receive packets from the rest of the Internet.
blocks.zh_html: 注意，箭头的方向并不告诉我们分组(packets)的发送方向。实际上，即使沿着有向边(directed edge)，分组也可以在两个方向上发送。客户通常向提供商付费，以获得向互联网其余部分发送和接收分组的能力。

blocks.en: AS Graphs are Acyclic
blocks.en_html: AS Graphs are Acyclic
blocks.zh_html: AS 图是无环的(AS Graphs are Acyclic)

blocks.en: The graph of customer-provider relationships is acyclic. The graph does not contain any cycles consisting of directed edges.
blocks.en_html: The graph of customer-provider relationships is acyclic. The graph does not contain any cycles consisting of directed edges.
blocks.zh_html: 客户-提供商关系(customer-provider relationships)的图是无环的(acyclic)。该图不包含由有向边(directed edges)组成的环(cycles)。

blocks.en: This acyclic property exists because of the real-world implications of having a cycle. In real life, a cycle would mean that A pays B, B pays C, and then C pays A, and it doesn’t make sense for money to flow from somebody back to themselves. Also, this cycle would mean that A provides service to C, which provides service to B, which provides service to A. It also doesn’t make sense for somebody to provide connectivity to themselves.
blocks.en_html: This acyclic property exists because of the real-world implications of having a cycle. In real life, a cycle would mean that A pays B, B pays C, and then C pays A, and it doesn’t make sense for money to flow from somebody back to themselves. Also, this cycle would mean that A provides service to C, which provides service to B, which provides service to A. It also doesn’t make sense for somebody to provide connectivity to themselves.
blocks.zh_html: 这种无环性质(acyclic property)源于现实中存在环的含义。在现实中，一个环意味着 A 付钱给 B，B 付钱给 C，然后 C 又付钱给 A，钱流回自己身上是不合理的。同样，这个环还意味着 A 为 C 提供服务，C 为 B 提供服务，B 又为 A 提供服务。自己为自己提供连接也是不合理的。

blocks.en: To use an analogy, imagine if you paid UC Berkeley tuition for classes, then UC Berkeley paid the UC system for classes, and then the UC system paid you for classes. This business relationship doesn’t make any sense!
blocks.en_html: To use an analogy, imagine if you paid UC Berkeley tuition for classes, then UC Berkeley paid the UC system for classes, and then the UC system paid you for classes. This business relationship doesn’t make any sense!
blocks.zh_html: 打个比方，想象一下你向 UC Berkeley 付学费上课，然后 UC Berkeley 向加州大学系统付学费上课，然后加州大学系统又向你付学费上课。这种商业关系毫无意义！

blocks.en: Note that the acyclic property only applies to customer-provider relationships. It is okay if peering relationships form a cycle. For example, it’s okay if A-B, B-C, and C-A are all peers. None of them are sending each other money, so we don’t have an ill-defined business relationship.
blocks.en_html: Note that the acyclic property only applies to customer-provider relationships. It is okay if peering relationships form a cycle. For example, it’s okay if A-B, B-C, and C-A are all peers. None of them are sending each other money, so we don’t have an ill-defined business relationship.
blocks.zh_html: 注意，无环性质只适用于客户-提供商关系(customer-provider relationships)。对等关系(peering relationships)形成环是可以的。例如，A-B、B-C 和 C-A 都是对等体是没问题的。它们之间没有任何金钱往来，所以不存在不明确的商业关系。

blocks.en: Provider Hierarchy and Tier 1 ASes
blocks.en_html: Provider Hierarchy and Tier 1 ASes
blocks.zh_html: 提供商层次结构和 Tier 1 AS(Provider Hierarchy and Tier 1 ASes)

blocks.en: A consequence of the graph being acyclic is, we can form a hierarchy of providers. In other words, we can arrange the nodes such that all the arrows point downward. The stub ASes are at the bottom, the providers are at the top. Service flows from higher to lower nodes. The lower nodes pay money up to higher nodes.
blocks.en_html: A consequence of the graph being acyclic is, we can form a hierarchy of providers. In other words, we can arrange the nodes such that all the arrows point downward. The stub ASes are at the bottom, the providers are at the top. Service flows from higher to lower nodes. The lower nodes pay money up to higher nodes.
blocks.zh_html: 图是无环的一个结果是，我们可以形成提供商的层次结构(hierarchy)。换句话说，我们可以排列节点，使得所有箭头都指向下方。末梢 AS(stub ASes)在底部，提供商在顶部。服务从较高节点流向较低节点。较低节点向较高节点付钱。

blocks.en: At the very top of the hierarchy, there are Tier 1 autonomous systems, which have no providers (no incoming edges). Every Tier 1 AS has a peering relationship with every other Tier 1 AS.
blocks.en_html: At the very top of the hierarchy, there are Tier 1 autonomous systems, which have no providers (no incoming edges). Every Tier 1 AS has a peering relationship with every other Tier 1 AS.
blocks.zh_html: 在层次结构的顶端，有第一层自治系统(Tier 1 autonomous systems)，它们没有提供商（没有入边）。每个 Tier 1 AS 与所有其他 Tier 1 AS 都有对等关系(peering relationship)。

blocks.en: A consequence of this hierarchy is: Every non-Tier 1 AS has at least one provider (incoming edge). This makes sense in real life, since you have to pay somebody to offer you connectivity.
blocks.en_html: A consequence of this hierarchy is: Every non-Tier 1 AS has at least one provider (incoming edge). This makes sense in real life, since you have to pay somebody to offer you connectivity.
blocks.zh_html: 这个层次结构的一个后果是：每个非 Tier 1 AS 至少有一个提供商（入边）。这在现实中是有意义的，因为你必须付钱给某人来为你提供连接。

blocks.en: In this hierarchy, starting from any AS, and following the uphill chain of providers, always leads to a Tier 1 AS. This also makes sense in real life. The Tier 1 ASes all peering with each other is why the entire Internet is connected (as opposed to, say, two disconnected subgraphs representing two separate Internets where you can only talk to hosts in your own half). In order to guarantee having a path to every other AS in the graph, every AS must have a path upwards that eventually leads to a Tier 1 AS.
blocks.en_html: In this hierarchy, starting from any AS, and following the uphill chain of providers, always leads to a Tier 1 AS. This also makes sense in real life. The Tier 1 ASes all peering with each other is why the entire Internet is connected (as opposed to, say, two disconnected subgraphs representing two separate Internets where you can only talk to hosts in your own half). In order to guarantee having a path to every other AS in the graph, every AS must have a path upwards that eventually leads to a Tier 1 AS.
blocks.zh_html: 在这个层次结构中，从任何 AS 出发，沿着提供商的上行链路上行，最终都会到达一个 Tier 1 AS。这在现实中也有意义。所有 Tier 1 AS 互相之间都是对等关系，这就是为什么整个互联网是连通的（而不是两个不连通的子图，代表两个独立的互联网，你只能与自己一半的主机通信）。为了保证图中到每个其他 AS 都有路径，每个 AS 必须有一条上行路径，最终到达一个 Tier 1 AS。

There are around 20 ASes that are Tier 1 or nearly Tier 1 in real life. These Tier 1 ASes usually own infrastructure spanning multiple continents (e.g. undersea cables).
blocks.zh_html: 现实中一些 Tier 1 AS 的例子包括 AT&T 和 Verizon（美国）、France Telecom 和 Telecom Italia（欧洲）、以及 NTT Communications（日本）。现实中有大约 20 个 AS 是 Tier 1 或接近 Tier 1。这些 Tier 1 AS 通常拥有横跨多个大洲的基础设施（例如海底光缆）。

blocks.en: The hierarchy structure of the AS graph is defined by real-world business and political motivations. In theory, it would be possible to draw an AS graph that looks like a tree, with a single Tier 1 AS at the root providing services to every stub AS. However, this means that a single real-life entity controls the entire world’s Internet access, which may be undesirable for political reasons.
blocks.en_html: The hierarchy structure of the AS graph is defined by real-world business and political motivations. In theory, it would be possible to draw an AS graph that looks like a tree, with a single Tier 1 AS at the root providing services to every stub AS. However, this means that a single real-life entity controls the entire world’s Internet access, which may be undesirable for political reasons.
blocks.zh_html: AS 图的层次结构由现实的商业和政治动机决定。理论上，我们可以画一个树状的 AS 图，由一个 Tier 1 AS 作为根节点，为所有末梢 AS(stub AS)提供服务。然而，这意味着单一的实体控制着全世界的互联网接入，这可能出于政治原因是不理想的。

blocks.en: Policy-Based Routing
blocks.en_html: Policy-Based Routing
blocks.zh_html: 基于策略的路由(Policy-Based Routing)

blocks.en: Recall that in intra-domain routing, our goal was to find paths that are valid (no loops and no dead-ends) and good (least cost).
blocks.en_html: Recall that in intra-domain routing, our goal was to find paths that are valid (no loops and no dead-ends) and good (least cost).
blocks.zh_html: 回想一下，在域内路由(intra-domain routing)中，我们的目标是找到有效(valid)（无环且无死胡同）且好(good)（最小成本）的路径(paths)。

blocks.en: In inter-domain routing, we still want paths to be valid. However, unlike in intra-domain routing, where there was nothing special about one router over another, each autonomous system has its own business goals and relationships with other ASes (e.g. customer, provider, peer). Therefore, we will need to re-define “good” to reflect the real-world business goals and preferences of ASes.
blocks.en_html: In inter-domain routing, we still want paths to be valid. However, unlike in intra-domain routing, where there was nothing special about one router over another, each autonomous system has its own business goals and relationships with other ASes (e.g. customer, provider, peer). Therefore, we will need to re-define “good” to reflect the real-world business goals and preferences of ASes.
blocks.zh_html: 在域间路由(inter-domain routing)中，我们仍然希望路径是有效的。然而，与域内路由不同的是，域内路由中一台路由器并不比另一台特殊；而每个自治系统(autonomous system)都有自己的商业目标以及与其他 AS 的关系（如客户、提供商、对等体）。因此，我们需要重新定义"好"以反映 AS 在现实中的商业目标和偏好。

blocks.en: In order to allow each AS to carry traffic in a way that’s compatible with its real-world goals, our routing protocol will allow each AS to set its own policy. Then, the paths computed by the protocol should properly respect each AS’s policy.
blocks.en_html: In order to allow each AS to carry traffic in a way that’s compatible with its real-world goals, our routing protocol will allow each AS to set its own policy. Then, the paths computed by the protocol should properly respect each AS’s policy.
blocks.zh_html: 为了让每个 AS 以与其现实目标兼容的方式承载流量，我们的路由协议将允许每个 AS 设置自己的策略(policy)。然后，协议计算出的路径应适当尊重每个 AS 的策略。

blocks.en: In theory, ASes can set any sort of policy that they like, although standard conventions do exist (which we’ll discuss next). Here are some examples of policies that an AS could set:
blocks.en_html: In theory, ASes can set any sort of policy that they like, although standard conventions do exist (which we’ll discuss next). Here are some examples of policies that an AS could set:
blocks.zh_html: 理论上，AS 可以设置任何它们喜欢的策略，尽管确实存在一些标准惯例（我们接下来会讨论）。以下是 AS 可能设置的一些策略示例：

blocks.en: “I don’t want to carry AS#2046’s traffic through my network.” (Defining how I will handle traffic from other ASes.)
blocks.en_html: “I don’t want to carry AS#2046’s traffic through my network.” (Defining how I will handle traffic from other ASes.)
blocks.zh_html: "我不想让 AS#2046 的流量经过我的网络。"（定义我将如何处理来自其他 AS 的流量。）

blocks.en: “I prefer if my traffic was carried by AS#10 instead of AS#4.” (Defining how other ASes should handle my traffic.)
blocks.en_html: “I prefer if my traffic was carried by AS#10 instead of AS#4.” (Defining how other ASes should handle my traffic.)
blocks.zh_html: "我希望我的流量由 AS#10 而非 AS#4 来承载。"（定义其他 AS 应如何处理我的流量。）

blocks.en: “Don’t send my traffic through AS#54 unless absolutely necessary.”
blocks.en_html: “Don’t send my traffic through AS#54 unless absolutely necessary.”
blocks.zh_html: "除非绝对必要，否则不要将我的流量发送经过 AS#54。"

blocks.en: “I prefer AS#12 on weekdays, and AS#13 on weekends.” (Policies can change over time!)
blocks.en_html: “I prefer AS#12 on weekdays, and AS#13 on weekends.” (Policies can change over time!)
blocks.zh_html: "我更喜欢在工作日使用 AS#12，在周末使用 AS#13。"（策略可以随时间变化！）

blocks.en: The routing protocol doesn’t care why the AS has these preferences. Perhaps I’m refusing to carry traffic from AS#2046 because it’s a rival company, but the protocol doesn’t need to know that.
blocks.en_html: The routing protocol doesn’t care why the AS has these preferences. Perhaps I’m refusing to carry traffic from AS#2046 because it’s a rival company, but the protocol doesn’t need to know that.
blocks.zh_html: 路由协议不关心 AS 为什么有这些偏好。也许我拒绝承载来自 AS#2046 的流量是因为它是竞争对手，但协议不需要知道这一点。

blocks.en: Our least-cost routing protocols so far have no way of supporting these policies. Least-cost was a global minimization problem, where every router was trying to solve the same problem. By contrast, in policy-based routing, each AS only cares about its own policy, and there isn’t a global problem that everybody is cooperating to solve.
blocks.en_html: Our least-cost routing protocols so far have no way of supporting these policies. Least-cost was a global minimization problem, where every router was trying to solve the same problem. By contrast, in policy-based routing, each AS only cares about its own policy, and there isn’t a global problem that everybody is cooperating to solve.
blocks.zh_html: 我们目前的最小成本路由协议没有办法支持这些策略。最小成本是一个全局最小化问题，每台路由器都在尝试解决同一个问题。相比之下，在基于策略的路由(policy-based routing)中，每个 AS 只关心自己的策略，不存在一个大家合作解决的全局问题。

blocks.en: Gao-Rexford Rules for Routing Policies
blocks.en_html: Gao-Rexford Rules for Routing Policies
blocks.zh_html: 路由策略的 Gao-Rexford 规则(Gao-Rexford Rules for Routing Policies)

blocks.en: Although our routing protocol allows each AS to set any arbitrary policy they like, in practice, most ASes set their policies according to some standard conventions, known as the Gao-Rexford rules. These conventions are based in the assumption that real-world organizations like making money, and dislike losing money.
blocks.en_html: Although our routing protocol allows each AS to set any arbitrary policy they like, in practice, most ASes set their policies according to some standard conventions, known as the Gao-Rexford rules. These conventions are based in the assumption that real-world organizations like making money, and dislike losing money.
blocks.zh_html: 尽管我们的路由协议允许每个 AS 设置任意策略，但在实践中，大多数 AS 根据一些标准惯例设置策略，这些惯例被称为Gao-Rexford 规则(Gao-Rexford rules)。这些惯例基于一个假设：现实中的组织喜欢赚钱，不喜欢亏钱。

blocks.en: There are two broad rules that ASes typically follow. First, when an AS has a choice of multiple routes, the AS prefers to forward packets to the most profitable next hop. Specifically, the AS prefers a route with a next hop that is a customer. If there are no such routes, the AS prefers a route with a next hop that is a peer. The AS will only select a route with a next hop that is a provider if it’s forced to do so, because there are no better routes.
blocks.en_html: There are two broad rules that ASes typically follow. First, when an AS has a choice of multiple routes, the AS prefers to forward packets to the most profitable next hop. Specifically, the AS prefers a route with a next hop that is a customer. If there are no such routes, the AS prefers a route with a next hop that is a peer. The AS will only select a route with a next hop that is a provider if it’s forced to do so, because there are no better routes.
blocks.zh_html: AS 通常遵循两个主要规则。第一，当一个 AS 有多条路由可以选择时，它倾向于将分组转发给最有利可图的下一跳(next hop)。具体来说，AS 优先选择下一跳是客户(customer)的路由。如果没有这样的路由，则优先选择下一跳是对等体(peer)的路由。只有在没有更好的路由时，AS 才会选择下一跳是提供商(provider)的路由。

blocks.en: This principle dictates the routes that the AS selects. You can think of this principle as a preference-based version of selecting paths in the distance-vector protocol. Instead of selecting the shortest route I know about, I select the route where the next hop makes me money (customer best), or saves me money (if no customers, then peer), and avoids losing money (if no customers or peers, then provider).
blocks.en_html: This principle dictates the routes that the AS selects. You can think of this principle as a preference-based version of selecting paths in the distance-vector protocol. Instead of selecting the shortest route I know about, I select the route where the next hop makes me money (customer best), or saves me money (if no customers, then peer), and avoids losing money (if no customers or peers, then provider).
blocks.zh_html: 这一原则决定了 AS 选择哪条路由。你可以把这个原则理解为距离向量协议(distance-vector protocol)中路径选择的基于偏好的版本。不选择我知道的最短路径，而是选择下一跳能让我赚钱（客户最好），或帮我省钱（没有客户则选对等体），并且避免亏钱（没有客户或对等体时选择提供商）的路径。

blocks.en: Second, ASes only carry traffic if they’re getting paid for it. There’s no incentive for ASes to perform free labor. This principle dictates the paths that the AS is willing to participate in. You can think of this principle as a more restrictive version of announcing paths in the distance-vector protocol. Instead of advertising a route to every neighbor, allowing anybody to forward packets through me, I only advertise routes in which I’m paid to forward packets.
blocks.en_html: Second, ASes only carry traffic if they’re getting paid for it. There’s no incentive for ASes to perform free labor. This principle dictates the paths that the AS is willing to participate in. You can think of this principle as a more restrictive version of announcing paths in the distance-vector protocol. Instead of advertising a route to every neighbor, allowing anybody to forward packets through me, I only advertise routes in which I’m paid to forward packets.
blocks.zh_html: 第二，AS 只有在自己能获得报酬时才承载流量。AS 没有动力去提供免费劳动。这一原则决定了 AS 愿意参与哪些路径。你可以把这个原则理解为距离向量协议中路径通告的更具限制性的版本。不向所有邻居通告路由从而允许任何人通过我转发分组，我只通告那些我因转发分组而获得报酬的路由。

blocks.en: A consequence of this second principle is: As an AS, the traffic I carry should come from a customer, or go to a customer. In other words, for any route going through me, one of my neighbors must be a customer.
blocks.en_html: A consequence of this second principle is: As an AS, the traffic I carry should come from a customer, or go to a customer. In other words, for any route going through me, one of my neighbors must be a customer.
blocks.zh_html: 第二个原则的一个结果是：作为一个 AS，我承载的流量应该来自一个客户，或者去往一个客户。换句话说，对于任何经过我的路由，我的一个邻居必须是客户。

blocks.en: Let’s go through all the specific cases.
blocks.en_html: Let’s go through all the specific cases.
blocks.zh_html: 让我们看看所有具体的情况。

blocks.en: Routes where both of my neighbors are customers are good, because I am getting paid by the two customers to forward packets.
blocks.en_html: Routes where both of my neighbors are customers are good, because I am getting paid by the two customers to forward packets.
blocks.zh_html: 我的两个邻居都是客户的路由是好的，因为两个客户都在为我转发分组付费。

blocks.en: Similarly, routes where one of my neighbors is a customer, and one of my neighbors is a peer are good, because even though the peer doesn’t pay me, the customer does.
blocks.en_html: Similarly, routes where one of my neighbors is a customer, and one of my neighbors is a peer are good, because even though the peer doesn’t pay me, the customer does.
blocks.zh_html: 类似地，一个邻居是客户，另一个邻居是对等体的路由也是好的，因为即使对等体不付钱给我，客户会付。

blocks.en: Routes where one of my neighbors is a customer, and the other is a provider are good. At first, it might seem like this path is bad, because the customer is paying me, and then I’m paying the provider. Isn’t it possible that I make no money, or lose money from this transaction? That may be true, but if we didn’t participate in these routes, we would be a useless AS with no customers. An AS’s job is to give connectivity to its users, and participating in these customer-AS-provider routes unlocks more routes to the rest of the Internet.
blocks.en_html: Routes where one of my neighbors is a customer, and the other is a provider are good. At first, it might seem like this path is bad, because the customer is paying me, and then I’m paying the provider. Isn’t it possible that I make no money, or lose money from this transaction? That may be true, but if we didn’t participate in these routes, we would be a useless AS with no customers. An AS’s job is to give connectivity to its users, and participating in these customer-AS-provider routes unlocks more routes to the rest of the Internet.
blocks.zh_html: 一个邻居是客户，另一个是提供商的路由也是好的。乍一看，这条路径似乎不好，因为客户付钱给我，然后我又付钱给提供商。难道我可能从这笔交易中赚不到钱，甚至亏钱吗？这可能是真的，但如果我们不参与这些路由，我们就会成为一个没有客户的无用 AS。AS 的职责是给它的用户提供连接，参与这些客户-AS-提供商路由可以解锁通往互联网其他部分的更多路由。

blocks.en: Routes where both of my neighbors are peers are bad, because neither side is paying me to forward packets.
blocks.en_html: Routes where both of my neighbors are peers are bad, because neither side is paying me to forward packets.
blocks.zh_html: 我的两个邻居都是对等体的路由是坏的，因为两边都不付钱给我转发分组。

blocks.en: More generally, peers do not provide transit between other peers. Thinking in terms of the hierarchy structure, a path should not stay at a given level for multiple hops.
blocks.en_html: More generally, peers do not provide transit between other peers. Thinking in terms of the hierarchy structure, a path should not stay at a given level for multiple hops.
blocks.zh_html: 更一般地说，对等体(peers)不在其他对等体之间提供中转(transit)。从层次结构的角度来看，一条路径不应当在同一层级停留多跳。

blocks.en: Routes where one of my neighbors is a peer, and the other is a provider are also bad, because again, neither side is paying me to forward packets.
blocks.en_html: Routes where one of my neighbors is a peer, and the other is a provider are also bad, because again, neither side is paying me to forward packets.
blocks.zh_html: 一个邻居是对等体，另一个是提供商的路由也是坏的，因为同样两边都不付钱给我转发分组。

blocks.en: More generally, if an AS has a peering link, that link will only carry traffic to/from its own customers. In other words, when packets arrive at B via that peering link, B’s only profitable option is to forward the packet to a customer (not a provider, and not another peer). Similarly, packets from customers can be forwarded through the peering link (customer pays), but packets from providers and peers cannot be forwarded through the peering link (nobody is paying).
blocks.en_html: More generally, if an AS has a peering link, that link will only carry traffic to/from its own customers. In other words, when packets arrive at B via that peering link, B’s only profitable option is to forward the packet to a customer (not a provider, and not another peer). Similarly, packets from customers can be forwarded through the peering link (customer pays), but packets from providers and peers cannot be forwarded through the peering link (nobody is paying).
blocks.zh_html: 更一般地说，如果一个 AS 有一条对等链路(peering link)，该链路只承载来往于其自身客户的流量。换句话说，当分组通过对等链路到达 B 时，B 唯一有利可图的选择是将分组转发给一个客户（而不是提供商或其他对等体）。类似地，来自客户的分组可以通过对等链路转发（客户付费），但来自提供商和对等体的分组不能通过对等链路转发（没人付钱）。

blocks.en: Similarly, routes where both of my neighbors are providers are bad, because I have to pay both sides to forward the packet, and nobody is paying me to do this.
blocks.en_html: Similarly, routes where both of my neighbors are providers are bad, because I have to pay both sides to forward the packet, and nobody is paying me to do this.
blocks.zh_html: 类似地，我的两个邻居都是提供商的路由是坏的，因为我必须向两边付钱来转发分组，而没人付钱给我做这件事。

blocks.en: Examples of Gao-Rexford Rules
blocks.en_html: Examples of Gao-Rexford Rules
blocks.zh_html: Gao-Rexford 规则示例(Examples of Gao-Rexford Rules)

blocks.en: The policy for selecting routes (customer best, provider worst), and the policy for announcing routes (only announce and participate in routes where one of my neighbors is a customer) will be used in our modified protocol to compute routes that respect each AS’s policy. We haven’t said how to compute routes yet, but given a route, we can check if it satisfies these two policies.
blocks.en_html: The policy for selecting routes (customer best, provider worst), and the policy for announcing routes (only announce and participate in routes where one of my neighbors is a customer) will be used in our modified protocol to compute routes that respect each AS’s policy. We haven’t said how to compute routes yet, but given a route, we can check if it satisfies these two policies.
blocks.zh_html: 选择路由的策略（客户最好，提供商最差）和通告路由的策略（只通告和参与至少有一个邻居是客户的路由）将被用于我们修改后的协议中，以计算出尊重每个 AS 策略的路由。我们还没说如何计算路由，但给定一条路由，我们可以检查它是否满足这两个策略。

blocks.en: In this example, suppose that a computer in D (a stub AS) wants to talk to a computer in E (another stub AS). D and E might want to exchange messages (remember, arrows represent customer/provider relationships, not direction of packets).
blocks.en_html: In this example, suppose that a computer in D (a stub AS) wants to talk to a computer in E (another stub AS). D and E might want to exchange messages (remember, arrows represent customer/provider relationships, not direction of packets).
blocks.zh_html: 在这个例子中，假设 D（一个末梢 AS）中的一台电脑想与 E（另一个末梢 AS）中的一台电脑通信。D 和 E 可能想要交换消息（记住，箭头表示客户/提供商关系，而不是分组的发送方向）。

blocks.en: One possible path for the traffic is D, B, A, C, E (and reverse for messages from E to D).
blocks.en_html: One possible path for the traffic is D, B, A, C, E (and reverse for messages from E to D).
blocks.zh_html: 一条可能的流量路径是 D, B, A, C, E（对于从 E 到 D 的消息，反之亦然）。

blocks.en: Who is paying whom in this path? Since traffic is being sent along the D-B link, the customer (D) must pay the provider (B). Similarly, E must pay C, and B and C must both pay A.
blocks.en_html: Who is paying whom in this path? Since traffic is being sent along the D-B link, the customer (D) must pay the provider (B). Similarly, E must pay C, and B and C must both pay A.
blocks.zh_html: 谁在这条路径上付钱给谁？由于流量沿着 D-B 链路发送，客户(D)必须付钱给提供商(B)。类似地，E 必须付钱给 C，B 和 C 都必须付钱给 A。

blocks.en: Will the transit ASes A, B, and C agree to announce and participate in this route? Let’s check each of their neighbors.
blocks.en_html: Will the transit ASes A, B, and C agree to announce and participate in this route? Let’s check each of their neighbors.
blocks.zh_html: 中转 AS A、B 和 C 会同意通告并参与这条路由吗？让我们逐一检查它们的邻居。

blocks.en: A’s neighbors along this path are both customers, so A is making money, and thinks this path is good.
blocks.en_html: A’s neighbors along this path are both customers, so A is making money, and thinks this path is good.
blocks.zh_html: A 在这条路径上的邻居都是客户，所以 A 在赚钱，认为这条路径是好的。

blocks.en: B’s neighbors are a customer (D) and a provider (A). B is making money from the customer (D), and thinks this path is good. (Remember, paths with one customer neighbor and one provider neighbor are good, even if the AS has net profit of 0, because they enable greater connectivity.)
blocks.en_html: B’s neighbors are a customer (D) and a provider (A). B is making money from the customer (D), and thinks this path is good. (Remember, paths with one customer neighbor and one provider neighbor are good, even if the AS has net profit of 0, because they enable greater connectivity.)
blocks.zh_html: B 的邻居是一个客户(D)和一个提供商(A)。B 从客户(D)那里赚钱，认为这条路径是好的。（记住，有一个客户邻居和一个提供商邻居的路径是好的，即使 AS 的净利润为 0，因为它们实现了更大的连通性。）

blocks.en: Similarly, C has at least one customer neighbor (E), so it also thinks this route is good.
blocks.en_html: Similarly, C has at least one customer neighbor (E), so it also thinks this route is good.
blocks.zh_html: 类似地，C 至少有一个客户邻居(E)，所以它也认为这条路由是好的。

blocks.en: Instead of B and C both paying A, perhaps they choose to establish a peer relationship, which causes the AS graph to change:
blocks.en_html: Instead of B and C both paying A, perhaps they choose to establish a peer relationship, which causes the AS graph to change:
blocks.zh_html: B 和 C 不都付钱给 A，而是可能选择建立对等关系(peer relationship)，这会导致 AS 图发生变化：

blocks.en: Now, another possible path for the traffic is D, B, C, E. Now, D still needs to pay B, and E still has to pay C. However, B and C no longer need to pay A, and they don’t pay each other (peering relationship).
blocks.en_html: Now, another possible path for the traffic is D, B, C, E. Now, D still needs to pay B, and E still has to pay C. However, B and C no longer need to pay A, and they don’t pay each other (peering relationship).
blocks.zh_html: 现在，另一条可能的流量路径是 D, B, C, E。现在，D 仍然需要付钱给 B，E 仍然需要付钱给 C。然而，B 和 C 不再需要付钱给 A，她们也不付钱给对方（对等关系）。

blocks.en: Again, we can check if the transit ASes on this path, namely B and C, will agree to announce and participate in this route. B’s neighbors are a customer (D) and a provider (C). B is making money from the customer (D), and thinks this path is good. Similarly, C has at least one customer neighbor (E), so C also thinks this path is good.
blocks.en_html: Again, we can check if the transit ASes on this path, namely B and C, will agree to announce and participate in this route. B’s neighbors are a customer (D) and a provider (C). B is making money from the customer (D), and thinks this path is good. Similarly, C has at least one customer neighbor (E), so C also thinks this path is good.
blocks.zh_html: 同样，我们可以检查这条路径上的中转 AS，即 B 和 C，是否会同意通告并参与这条路由。B 的邻居是一个客户(D)和一个提供商(C)。B 从客户(D)那里赚钱，认为这条路径是好的。类似地，C 至少有一个客户邻居(E)，所以 C 也认为这条路径是好的。

blocks.en: We’ve just reasoned that there are two good paths that can be used to send messages from D to E. Now, B must decide to forward through either path B-A-C-E, or path B-C-E. Which path should B choose? According to our first principle, B prefers the most profitable path (not the shortest path). In B-A-C-E, the next hop is provider A (who we’d have to pay), and in B-C-E, the next hop is peer C (no payment needed). Therefore, B will select the path through C, giving final path D-B-C-E.
blocks.en_html: We’ve just reasoned that there are two good paths that can be used to send messages from D to E. Now, B must decide to forward through either path B-A-C-E, or path B-C-E. Which path should B choose? According to our first principle, B prefers the most profitable path (not the shortest path). In B-A-C-E, the next hop is provider A (who we’d have to pay), and in B-C-E, the next hop is peer C (no payment needed). Therefore, B will select the path through C, giving final path D-B-C-E.
blocks.zh_html: 我们已经推断出有两条好路径可以用来从 D 向 E 发送消息。现在，B 必须决定是通过路径 B-A-C-E 转发，还是通过路径 B-C-E 转发。B 应该选择哪条路径？根据我们的第一个原则，B 偏好最有利可图的路径（而不是最短路径）。在 B-A-C-E 中，下一跳是提供商 A（我们得付钱给他），而在 B-C-E 中，下一跳是对等体 C（无需付款）。因此，B 会选择经过 C 的路径，最终路径为 D-B-C-E。

blocks.en: Note: It seems like B and C are saving money with the additional peering relationship, so why wouldn’t every AS establish peer relationships to save money? In real life, establishing a link also requires installing physical infrastructure (e.g. laying cables underground), so there’s a cost trade-off to establishing new relationships between ASes, in exchange for cheaper routes.
blocks.en_html: Note: It seems like B and C are saving money with the additional peering relationship, so why wouldn’t every AS establish peer relationships to save money? In real life, establishing a link also requires installing physical infrastructure (e.g. laying cables underground), so there’s a cost trade-off to establishing new relationships between ASes, in exchange for cheaper routes.
blocks.zh_html: 注意：看起来 B 和 C 通过额外的对等关系(peering relationship)省了钱，那为什么不是每个 AS 都建立对等关系来省钱呢？在现实中，建立链路还需要安装物理基础设施（例如在地下铺设光缆），所以在 AS 之间建立新关系需要权衡成本，以换取更便宜的路由。

blocks.en: Routes are Valley-Free
blocks.en_html: Routes are Valley-Free
blocks.zh_html: 路由是无谷的(Routes are Valley-Free)

blocks.en: More generally, paths in the AS graph are always valley-free.
blocks.en_html: More generally, paths in the AS graph are always valley-free.
blocks.zh_html: 更一般地说，AS 图(graph)中的路径(paths)总是无谷的(valley-free)。

blocks.en: Thinking in terms of the hierarchy structure, if a path includes a lateral hop via a peering link, the immediate next hop needs to go downhill to a customer. The next hop cannot be lateral again (both neighbors peers), and the next hop cannot be uphill to a provider (peer and provider neighbors).
blocks.en_html: Thinking in terms of the hierarchy structure, if a path includes a lateral hop via a peering link, the immediate next hop needs to go downhill to a customer. The next hop cannot be lateral again (both neighbors peers), and the next hop cannot be uphill to a provider (peer and provider neighbors).
blocks.zh_html: 从层次结构的角度来看，如果一条路径包含经过对等链路(peering link)的水平跳，紧接着的下一跳需要下行到客户。下一跳不能再次是水平的（两个邻居都是对等体），也不能上行到提供商（对等体和提供商邻居）。

blocks.en: Thinking in terms of the hierarchy structure, if a path includes a downward hop from provider to customer, the immediate next hop must continue to go downhill to one of its customers. The next hop cannot be lateral again (neighbors are provider and peer), and the next hop cannot be uphill (neighbors are both providers).
blocks.en_html: Thinking in terms of the hierarchy structure, if a path includes a downward hop from provider to customer, the immediate next hop must continue to go downhill to one of its customers. The next hop cannot be lateral again (neighbors are provider and peer), and the next hop cannot be uphill (neighbors are both providers).
blocks.zh_html: 从层次结构的角度来看，如果一条路径包含从提供商到客户的下行跳，紧接着的下一跳必须继续下行到它的一个客户。下一跳不能再次是水平的（邻居是提供商和对等体），也不能上行（两个邻居都是提供商）。

blocks.en: If a downhill link must be followed by another downhill link, then we can conclude that as soon as you have a downhill link in a path, all subsequent links must also be downhill. A valley is a path that goes downhill, and then turns around to start going uphill. Paths cannot contain valleys, because once you start going downhill, you must continue downhill all the way to the destination.
blocks.en_html: If a downhill link must be followed by another downhill link, then we can conclude that as soon as you have a downhill link in a path, all subsequent links must also be downhill. A valley is a path that goes downhill, and then turns around to start going uphill. Paths cannot contain valleys, because once you start going downhill, you must continue downhill all the way to the destination.
blocks.zh_html: 如果一个下行链路必须跟着另一个下行链路，那么我们可以得出结论：一旦路径中有一个下行链路，所有后续链路也必须都是下行链路。谷(valley)是指一条路径先下行，然后掉头开始上行。路径不能包含谷，因为一旦你开始下行，你必须一直下行到目的地。

blocks.en: In summary, here are the rules we’ve derived (though it’s better to understand them in terms of respecting AS money preferences, instead of memorizing them):
blocks.en_html: In summary, here are the rules we’ve derived (though it’s better to understand them in terms of respecting AS money preferences, instead of memorizing them):
blocks.zh_html: 总结一下，以下是推导出的规则（不过最好从尊重 AS 金钱偏好的角度去理解，而不是死记硬背）：

blocks.en: An uphill link can be followed by peering link, a downhill link, or another uphill link. (If the previous hop pays me money, I’m happy to forward the packet to anybody.)
blocks.en_html: An uphill link can be followed by peering link, a downhill link, or another uphill link. (If the previous hop pays me money, I’m happy to forward the packet to anybody.)
blocks.zh_html: 上行链路可以跟着对等链路、下行链路或另一个上行链路。（如果上一跳付钱给我，我很乐意把分组转发给任何人。）

blocks.en: A peering link can only be followed by a downhill link. (If the previous hop isn’t paying me, I need the next hop to be a customer that pays me.)
blocks.en_html: A peering link can only be followed by a downhill link. (If the previous hop isn’t paying me, I need the next hop to be a customer that pays me.)
blocks.zh_html: 对等链路只能跟着下行链路。（如果上一跳不付钱给我，我需要下一跳是一个付钱给我的客户。）

blocks.en: A downhill link can only be followed by a downhill link. (If the previous hop is a provider I’m paying, I need the next hop to be a customer that pays me.)
blocks.en_html: A downhill link can only be followed by a downhill link. (If the previous hop is a provider I’m paying, I need the next hop to be a customer that pays me.)
blocks.zh_html: 下行链路只能跟着下行链路。（如果上一跳是我付钱给的提供商，我需要下一跳是一个付钱给我的客户。）

blocks.en: These rules mean that routes are always valley-free and single-peaked. A route can start 0 or more climbing uphill links. Eventually, it will reach a single peak, and traverse 0 or 1 peering links. Then, the route must start going downhill all the way to the destination (no more lateral or uphill moves).
blocks.en_html: These rules mean that routes are always valley-free and single-peaked. A route can start 0 or more climbing uphill links. Eventually, it will reach a single peak, and traverse 0 or 1 peering links. Then, the route must start going downhill all the way to the destination (no more lateral or uphill moves).
blocks.zh_html: 这些规则意味着路径(paths)总是无谷的(valley-free)且单峰的(single-peaked)。一条路径可以以 0 个或多个上行链路开始。最终，它会到达一个峰顶，并经过 0 或 1 个对等链路。然后，路径必须一路下行到目的地（不再有水平或上行移动）。

blocks.en: Paths cannot have valleys (going downhill and then turning to go back uphill). Also, paths cannot have lateral moves anywhere except the peak. As soon as you make a lateral move, you must turn around and go back down. You cannot continue traveling laterally or uphill.
blocks.en_html: Paths cannot have valleys (going downhill and then turning to go back uphill). Also, paths cannot have lateral moves anywhere except the peak. As soon as you make a lateral move, you must turn around and go back down. You cannot continue traveling laterally or uphill.
blocks.zh_html: 路径不能有谷（先下行然后掉头再上行）。此外，除峰顶外，路径不能有任何水平移动。一旦你做了水平移动，你必须掉头回去下行。你不能继续水平或上行。

blocks.en: ASes Want Autonomy and Privacy
blocks.en_html: ASes Want Autonomy and Privacy
blocks.zh_html: AS 需要自治权和隐私(ASes Want Autonomy and Privacy)

blocks.en: When designing a protocol for computing inter-domain routes, our protocol should respect the autonomy and privacy of each AS.
blocks.en_html: When designing a protocol for computing inter-domain routes, our protocol should respect the autonomy and privacy of each AS.
blocks.zh_html: 在设计用于计算域间路由(inter-domain routes)的协议时，我们的协议应尊重每个 AS 的自治权(autonomy)和隐私(privacy)。

blocks.en: ASes want autonomy, the freedom to choose their own arbitrary policies, without coordinating with other ASes, or worrying about what policies the protocol allows. In practice, the policies usually follow the money-based principles we described, but the protocol shouldn’t force the AS to follow any specific policy.
blocks.en_html: ASes want autonomy, the freedom to choose their own arbitrary policies, without coordinating with other ASes, or worrying about what policies the protocol allows. In practice, the policies usually follow the money-based principles we described, but the protocol shouldn’t force the AS to follow any specific policy.
blocks.zh_html: AS 需要自治权(autonomy)，即自由选择任意策略的权利，无需与其他 AS 协调，也无需担心协议允许什么策略。在实践中，策略通常遵循我们描述的基于金钱的原则，但协议不应该强制 AS 遵守任何特定策略。

blocks.en: ASes also want privacy. ASes don’t want to have to explicitly tell others in the network about their preferences and policies. For example, an AS shouldn’t need to explicitly tell everybody about whether its neighbors are peers, customers, or providers. This reflects real-world business strategies. As a company, you might not want to reveal information about your customers and providers to your rivals.
blocks.en_html: ASes also want privacy. ASes don’t want to have to explicitly tell others in the network about their preferences and policies. For example, an AS shouldn’t need to explicitly tell everybody about whether its neighbors are peers, customers, or providers. This reflects real-world business strategies. As a company, you might not want to reveal information about your customers and providers to your rivals.
blocks.zh_html: AS 也需要隐私(privacy)。AS 不希望必须明确告诉网络中的其他人它们的偏好和策略。例如，一个 AS 不需要明确告诉所有人它的邻居是对等体、客户还是提供商。这反映了现实的商业策略。作为一家公司，你可能不希望向竞争对手透露你的客户和提供商信息。

blocks.en: Note that our definition of privacy says that ASes shouldn’t need to explicitly reveal their policies. In practice, ASes still need to coordinate with the rest of the network to agree on paths through the network, so some amount of information leakage is inevitable. Reverse-engineering techniques exist to trace the routes packets are taking through the network.
blocks.en_html: Note that our definition of privacy says that ASes shouldn’t need to explicitly reveal their policies. In practice, ASes still need to coordinate with the rest of the network to agree on paths through the network, so some amount of information leakage is inevitable. Reverse-engineering techniques exist to trace the routes packets are taking through the network.
blocks.zh_html: 注意，我们对隐私的定义说 AS 不需要明确透露其策略。在实践中，AS 仍然需要与网络的其余部分协调以就网络路径达成一致，因此一定程度的的信息泄露是不可避免的。存在逆向工程技术来追踪分组经过网络的路径。

blocks.en: For example, it’s unavoidable that others on the network can discover what route a packet is taking. However, our protocol shouldn’t force an AS to tell the world “I liked this path more than this other path.” We also shouldn’t force an AS to disclose who their providers, peers, and customers are.
blocks.en_html: For example, it’s unavoidable that others on the network can discover what route a packet is taking. However, our protocol shouldn’t force an AS to tell the world “I liked this path more than this other path.” We also shouldn’t force an AS to disclose who their providers, peers, and customers are.
blocks.zh_html: 例如，网络中其他人发现分组走的是哪条路径是不可避免的。然而，我们的协议不应该强制 AS 告诉世界"我更喜欢这条路径而非那条路径。"我们也不应该强制 AS 披露谁是它的提供商、对等体和客户。
